Item 1.01 Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement

On
November 9, 2026, NRG Energy, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the “
Company
”), entered into a Purchase and Sale Agreement
(the “
Purchase Agreement
”), by and between the Company

and Orbit Acquisition Holdco,
LLC, a Delaware limited liability company and an affiliate of LS Power Equity Advisors, LLC (“
Buyer
”). Subject to the
terms and conditions of the Purchase Agreement, the Company has agreed to 
cause certain of its subsidiaries to 
sell
to Buyer all of the issued and outstanding equity interests in 
(i) Linebacker Power Funding, LLC, a Delaware limited liability
company, (ii) Jack County Power Development, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, (iii) Ravenswood Operations, LLC, a New York limited
liability company, (iv) Ravenswood Services, LLC, a New York limited liability company, (v) Ravenswood Holdings, LLC, a Delaware limited
liability company, (vi) Ravenswood Unit 40, LLC, a New York limited liability company, (vii) Ocean State Power, LLC, a Rhode Island limited
liability company, (viii) Wallingford Energy, LLC, a Connecticut limited liability company, and (ix) Rise Development, LLC, a Delaware
limited liability company (collectively, together with their respective direct and indirect subsidiaries, the “
Acquired Companies
”).
The acquisition of the equity interests, together with the other transactions contemplated by the Purchase Agreement, is referred to herein
as the “
Transaction
.”

Subject
to the terms and conditions of the Purchase Agreement, the aggregate purchase price for the Transaction will consist of $4.0 billion
in cash, subject to net working capital and other adjustments set forth in the Purchase Agreement.

The Purchase Agreement contains representations
and warranties customary for transactions of this type. The parties have agreed to various customary covenants and agreements, including,
among others, an agreement by the Company to cause the Acquired Companies to conduct their businesses in the ordinary course of business
in all material respects during the period between the execution of the Purchase Agreement and the closing of the Transaction (the “
Closing
”).
In addition, the Company, solely with respect to the Acquired Companies, has agreed to certain limitations on the operation of their respective
businesses during such period, as set forth more fully in the Purchase Agreement.

Subject to the terms
and limitations set forth in the Purchase Agreement, Buyer has agreed to take, and to cause certain of its affiliates to take, all actions
necessary to obtain the required governmental approvals as promptly as practicable and in any event before May 9, 2027 (as such date may
be extended pursuant to the Purchase Agreement, the “
End Date
”).

Consummation of the Transaction is subject to
customary closing conditions, including (i) the absence of any law or order that restrains, enjoins or otherwise prohibits the consummation
of the Transaction, (ii) the expiration or termination of the waiting period and the receipt of other required approvals under the
Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended, (iii) the receipt of all necessary approvals, waivers and rulings from
the United States Federal Energy Regulatory Commission and the New York State Public Service Commission, and (iv) other customary
closing conditions, including the accuracy of each party’s representations and warranties and each party’s compliance with
its covenants and agreements contained in the Purchase Agreement (subject in the case of this clause (iv) to certain materiality
qualifiers). The Transaction is not subject to a financing condition. The Closing is expected to occur in 2027, subject to, among other
things, the satisfaction of the foregoing conditions.

The Purchase Agreement provides customary termination
rights to the Company and Buyer, including the right of either party to terminate the Purchase Agreement if (i) a final, non-appealable
order prohibits consummation of the Transaction; (ii) the other party breaches certain representations, warranties or covenants in a manner
that would prevent the satisfaction of a closing condition, subject to applicable cure periods; or (iii) the Transaction has not been
consummated by the End Date. The End Date may be automatically extended for up to two successive 90-day periods in certain circumstances,
subject to the terms and limitations set forth in the Purchase Agreement.

Buyer will be required to pay the Company a termination
fee of $200 million if (i) the Company terminates the Purchase Agreement due to certain breaches by Buyer, subject to applicable cure
provisions, including Buyer’s failure to pursue required regulatory remedies; (ii) the Company terminates the Purchase Agreement
due to Buyer’s failure to consummate the Transaction when required; or (iii) either party terminates the Purchase Agreement following
the End Date when the Company would have been entitled to terminate the Purchase Agreement pursuant to either of the foregoing clauses.

In connection with the Closing, the parties will
enter into certain ancillary agreements, including a transition services agreement and other commercial agreements between certain Acquired
Companies and a subsidiary of the Company relating to power and fuel management, natural gas supply and transportation capacity management.

A
copy of the Purchase Agreement has been included to provide investors with information regarding its terms. It is not intended to provide
any other factual information about Buyer, the Company or the 
Acquired
 Companies. In particular,
the representations and warranties contained in the Purchase Agreement were made only for the purposes of the Purchase Agreement as of
the specific dates therein, and were solely for the benefit of the parties to the Purchase Agreement. The representations and warranties
contained in the Purchase Agreement may be subject to limitations agreed upon by the parties to the Purchase Agreement and are qualified
by information in confidential disclosure schedules provided in connection with the signing of the Purchase Agreement. These confidential
disclosure schedules contain information that modifies, qualifies and creates exceptions to the representations and warranties set forth
in the Purchase Agreement. Additionally, certain representations and warranties in the Purchase Agreement may be subject to a standard
of materiality provided for in the Purchase Agreement and have been used for the purpose of allocating risk among the parties, rather
than establishing matters of fact. Investors are not third-party beneficiaries under the Purchase Agreement and should not rely on the
representations, warranties and covenants or any descriptions thereof as characterizations of the actual state of facts or condition of
Buyer, the Company or any of their respective subsidiaries or affiliates. Moreover, information concerning the subject matter of the representations
and warranties may change after the date of the Purchase Agreement, which subsequent information may or may not be fully reflected in
the Company’s public disclosures.

The foregoing description of the Purchase Agreement
and the Transaction does not purport to be complete and is subject to, and qualified in its entirety by, the full text of the Purchase
Agreement attached hereto as Exhibit 2.1 to this Current Report on Form 8-K, which is incorporated into this Item 1.01 by reference.

Forward-Looking Statements

presented in this Current Report on Form 8-K includes forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act

relating to the proposed Transaction, the satisfaction or waiver of the conditions necessary for the Company to complete the Transaction,
